chapter: Chick Webb, Lucky Roberts, Alex Jackson
title: Trumpeters imitating Louis; being natural
summary: He says players tried to imitate Armstrong's high notes, and urges originality.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well, I didn't mind, because after all, that's what -- the fellows were going around, everybody was stealing -- the new trumpet players were trying to steal Louis' stuff, Louis Armstrong. And you used to see more trumpet players, they used to sing, sometimes, and had a little patch over their lip. Say, what's the matter with you, fellow? What you do, hit yourself? Cut your lip? Oh, no, man, I was just practicing.
Come to find out they were trying to hit those high notes like Louis used to hit.

And Louis hit them with ease. They were trying to squeeze them out. They'd split their lips and everything like that. I never believed in that. I believe, be yourself and be natural and you're much better appreciated. See, and Louis was natural. You can't beat that, originality in anything, because anything that comes along is just a copy of the original. It's imitation. But the original thing you can't beat. Like the soda, Coca-Cola. When I was a little tiny kid, I used to drink it. Still going strong. And you got Pepsi-Cola and you got this and you got all kinds of different kinds of sodas. Imitation. But Coca-Cola is the original.
